gist: Alberta voters are deciding whether to pursue a binding referendum on leaving Canada.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Albertans went to the polls to vote on whether to begin the legal process for a binding independence referendum. Premier Danielle Smith called the vote following pressure and a grassroots petition, though she opposes separation. Voters also faced nine additional referendum questions covering matters such as immigration, social programmes and judicial appointments.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Separatists argue Ottawa's environmental policies constrain Alberta's fossil fuel wealth. Conversely, opponents, including Prime Minister Mark Carney, warn an exit would trigger severe financial uncertainty, lost jobs, and billions in debt. Indigenous First Nations challenged the process in court, arguing treaties prevent Alberta from having the constitutional right to separate.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Officials will count ballots by hand, with the separation question tallied first and initial results expected early Tuesday. If approved, a binding referendum could take place as early as 2027.

gist: Hackers breached an older system of open source AI coding agent OpenCode.
The attack affected 1.4% of users of the online platform OpenCode Console.
Attackers ran up unauthorized charges on users' connected AI accounts.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Attackers breached an older system of OpenCode overnight, affecting 1.4% of OpenCode Console users. Developers reported unauthorized charges and spending alerts on their AI accounts. While OpenCode described it as a distillation attack, skeptics called that framing an overstretch and argued it was a straightforward breach.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The incident highlighted difficulties in defending against large-scale cyberattacks when AI model safety guardrails refuse to analyse malicious payloads needed for defence work. Anthropic, Google and OpenAI blocked or worked to restore exposed keys, while refunds for unauthorised charges are underway.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: OpenCode stated that the incident remains ongoing. The company has instructed affected users to revoke and replace their API keys directly with each provider.

Attackers carried out a large-scale attack while OpenCode faced ongoing security pressures.
